campaign.objective: The heater has just been cut. Is stopping heat enough, or must we escalate?
campaign.title: NIST intervention benchmark

data.answer: At recorded heater-off, apply the declared agent_threshold world model using only available observations. Apply its registered decision rule and action costs. If it selects observation, commit the 30 or 60 s watch, use only the paid recorded samples, then commit stand-down or escalation before revealing the outcome. Escalation is a risk classification; its physical efficacy was not measured. Recorded evidence: 0 unsafe, 19 missed rescues over 50 held-out trials (loco); mean decision cost 3.8; 7 unsafe, 12 missed rescues over 50 held-out trials (lofo); mean decision cost 16.4; 2 unsafe, 11 missed rescues over 50 held-out trials (prequential); mean decision cost 6.2.

system.title: NIST heating interruption, 77 single-cell trials
system.citation: Tam et al., Applied Thermal Engineering 298 (2026) 131107, Tables A1/A2
system.licence: NIST open licence; US public domain
system.sensor: One surface type-K thermocouple, 1 Hz, mid-height
system.decision_point: Heater cut reconstructed with 10 s thermocouple lag; optional paid 30/60 s recorded watch

amendment_registration.reason: Frozen baselines are comparators, not candidate learning strategies

protocol.heldout_cap_unit: screened agent candidate strategies; baseline comparators do not consume K

primary_test.name: paired two-sided sign-flip permutation
primary_test.correction_family: submitted screened agent candidates times registered baseline comparators

preregistration_reasons: Observation must be available under laboratory action costs
Unsafe-only McNemar has inadequate resolution with few discordances
Video markers support a 7 s heater-off lag sensitivity alongside default 10 s
Frozen baseline comparators are not candidate learning strategies
protocol.calibration_metric: five-bin expected calibration error, with an additional Brier guard

funnel.screen: inner LOCO on revealed training only
funnel.unit: Held-out candidate submission is the agent learning strategy; frozen baselines are comparators

protocol.target: recorded ignition after recorded heater-off; no suppression counterfactual
protocol.censoring: finite observation window; censored trials flagged and sensitivity reported

procedure.text: At recorded heater-off, apply the declared agent_threshold world model using only available observations. Apply its registered decision rule and action costs. If it selects observation, commit the 30 or 60 s watch, use only the paid recorded samples, then commit stand-down or escalation before revealing the outcome. Escalation is a risk classification; its physical efficacy was not measured. Recorded evidence: 0 unsafe, 19 missed rescues over 50 held-out trials (loco); mean decision cost 3.8; 7 unsafe, 12 missed rescues over 50 held-out trials (lofo); mean decision cost 16.4; 2 unsafe, 11 missed rescues over 50 held-out trials (prequential); mean decision cost 6.2.
limits: Factual recorded heater-off only; suppression efficacy and alternative stop times were not observed
50 interrupted traces in one NIST study; a case study, not a validated fire-safety procedure
One surface thermocouple; internal state unmeasured; event reconstruction uses a 10 s lag
Censored rescues and inferred heater-off times; no indefinite stability claim
LOFO is a known transfer failure; no packs, other cell makes, powers or abuse modes
A supported performance count describes observed errors; it does not prove a safe stand-down guarantee
